classification_system.purpose: A small, auditable model-reconstructed view for testing domain-to-discipline-to-atomic-discipline classification in Mathematics.
classification_system.scope: Mathematics only; disciplinary and subdisciplinary organization, not a complete subject classification and not a syllabus.
classification_system.license: Internal project artifact; external sources retain their own terms.
limitations: This is a pilot synthesis, not an immutable copy of MSC2020 or any other official hierarchy.
The tree uses one practical parent per node; mathematical overlap is not denied and should be represented by graph crosswalks in a later phase.
Atomic discipline means a useful leaf for classification and review, not an irreducible unit of mathematical knowledge.
No human subject-matter review has been recorded for this artifact.

level_definitions.discipline: A broad mathematical field with a stable research and teaching identity.
level_definitions.subdiscipline: A named field that narrows a discipline without being a single topic or technique.
level_definitions.atomic_discipline: A leaf field with a coherent boundary, recognizable literature, and a useful independent classification target.

tree_rules: Every non-root node has exactly one tree parent in this pilot.
Every tree edge is represented once in relations and points from parent to child.
Leaves are intentionally limited to fields that can be reviewed as coherent units.
A confidence score expresses classification confidence; it does not replace provenance or review state.

aliases.label: Mathematical sciences (narrow pilot use)
aliases.scope: Not equivalent to the full mathematical sciences.

nodes.definition: The formal study of quantity, structure, space, change, uncertainty, and patterns through abstraction, deduction, and proof.
scope_excludes: Physics, computer science, and engineering as disciplines in their own right

nodes.definition: The study of algebraic structures, operations, equations, and the relationships preserved by algebraic transformations.
scope_includes: Number theory as a pilot subdiscipline
scope_excludes: Numerical computation as an engineering practice

nodes.definition: The study of limits, continuity, approximation, infinite processes, and functions of real or complex variables.
scope_includes: Real and complex analysis in broader classifications
scope_excludes: Discrete algorithms as a primary subject

nodes.definition: The mathematical study of uncertainty, random phenomena, data variation, inference, and decision under uncertainty.
scope_excludes: Business analytics and data engineering as professional practices

nodes.definition: The study of finite, countable, combinatorial, graph-based, and symbolic structures, including foundational discrete reasoning.
scope_excludes: Software engineering as a professional field

nodes.definition: The study of spatial form, geometric relationships, invariants, and spaces described synthetically, analytically, or differentially.
scope_excludes: Computer graphics implementation as an engineering practice

nodes.definition: The study of vector spaces, linear maps, matrices, systems of linear equations, and their algebraic invariants.
scope_excludes: General nonlinear algebraic geometry

nodes.definition: The study of integers, prime numbers, congruences, Diophantine problems, and arithmetic structures.
scope_includes: Elementary, algebraic, and analytic number theory
scope_excludes: Numerical number formatting

nodes.definition: The study of change, accumulation, limits, derivatives, integrals, and their extensions to several variables and vector fields.
scope_excludes: Numerical analysis implementation details

nodes.definition: The mathematical theory of random experiments, events, random variables, distributions, dependence, and stochastic evolution.
scope_excludes: Descriptive reporting without a probabilistic model

nodes.definition: The mathematical study of data-generating mechanisms, estimation, testing, prediction, experimental design, and uncertainty quantification.
scope_excludes: Data collection operations and business intelligence tooling

nodes.definition: The study of finite and countable arrangements, selections, configurations, enumeration, and extremal structure.
scope_excludes: General optimization software

nodes.definition: The study of graphs, networks, connectivity, paths, cycles, coloring, and structural properties of discrete relational systems.
scope_excludes: Network administration as an IT practice

nodes.definition: The study of formal languages, proof, definability, computability, models, and foundational mathematical structures.
scope_excludes: Informal reasoning pedagogy

nodes.definition: The study of points, lines, angles, figures, congruence, similarity, and metric relationships in Euclidean space.
scope_excludes: Differential geometry of manifolds

nodes.definition: The study of geometric objects and relationships through coordinates, equations, transformations, and algebraic representation.
scope_excludes: General algebraic geometry

nodes.definition: The study of smooth curves, surfaces, manifolds, metrics, and geometric properties using differential and analytic methods.
scope_excludes: Differential calculus as a general theory of functions

nodes.definition: The study of vector spaces, subspaces, bases, dimension, linear maps, kernels, images, and canonical linear constructions.
scope_excludes: Nonlinear maps as the primary object

nodes.definition: The study of matrices, determinants, canonical forms, eigenstructure, matrix decompositions, and matrix invariants.
scope_excludes: Numerical linear algebra software engineering

nodes.definition: The study of existence, uniqueness, structure, and solution methods for systems of linear equations and related operator equations.
scope_excludes: Nonlinear differential equation solving

nodes.definition: The study of divisibility, congruences, primes, arithmetic functions, and integer properties using elementary or classical methods.
scope_excludes: Algebraic number fields as the primary framework

nodes.definition: The study of algebraic numbers, number fields, ideals, valuations, and arithmetic properties of algebraic extensions.
scope_excludes: General abstract algebra without arithmetic focus

nodes.definition: The study of arithmetic questions using analytic functions, complex analysis, asymptotic methods, and estimates.
scope_excludes: Real analysis without arithmetic questions

nodes.definition: The study of polynomial or related equations whose solutions are sought in integers, rational numbers, or other arithmetic domains.
scope_excludes: Numerical root finding over the reals

nodes.definition: The study of rates of change, derivatives, local approximation, extrema, and differential behavior of functions.
scope_excludes: Integration as the primary operation

nodes.definition: The study of accumulation, definite and indefinite integrals, integration theorems, and areas or quantities obtained by integration.
scope_excludes: Measure theory in its full generality

nodes.definition: The study of limits, derivatives, integrals, and optimization for functions of several real variables.
scope_excludes: Abstract manifold theory as the primary setting

nodes.definition: The study of scalar and vector fields, line and surface integrals, and differential operators in Euclidean spaces.
scope_excludes: General vector space theory without calculus

nodes.definition: The axioms, events, sigma-algebras, probability measures, conditional probability, and independence underlying probability theory.
scope_excludes: Statistical estimation from observed samples

nodes.definition: The study of random variables, probability distributions, expectations, moments, dependence, and transformations.
scope_excludes: Time-indexed stochastic evolution as the primary object

nodes.definition: The study of random processes indexed by time or another parameter, including dependence, paths, and long-run behavior.
scope_excludes: Static distributions without an indexing process

nodes.definition: The study of estimating unknown quantities, testing hypotheses, and quantifying uncertainty from data under statistical models.
scope_excludes: Descriptive summaries without inference

nodes.definition: The study of conditional relationships and prediction using regression models, including linear and generalized models.
scope_excludes: Machine-learning engineering outside statistical modeling

nodes.definition: The study of principled assignment, control, randomization, and analysis plans for learning causal or comparative information from experiments.
scope_excludes: Laboratory operations without a statistical design question

nodes.definition: The study of statistical reasoning that combines prior distributions with likelihoods to obtain posterior uncertainty and decisions.
scope_excludes: Philosophical debate about probability without statistical modeling

nodes.definition: The study of counting finite structures, generating functions, recurrence relations, and exact enumeration methods.
scope_excludes: Continuous probability distributions

nodes.definition: The study of maximum or minimum size and structure of finite configurations subject to combinatorial constraints.
scope_excludes: Continuous optimization without a finite combinatorial structure

nodes.definition: The study of graph structure through connectivity, minors, decompositions, coloring, cycles, and structural invariants.
scope_excludes: Operational network monitoring

nodes.definition: The study of algorithms whose inputs, outputs, or correctness properties are expressed using graph structures.
scope_excludes: General software engineering practices

nodes.definition: The study of sets, membership, cardinality, ordinal structure, axioms, and constructions used as mathematical foundations.
scope_excludes: Database set operations as an implementation topic

nodes.definition: The study of which functions and problems can be computed, with what resources, and by which formal models of computation.
scope_excludes: Application programming and software delivery

nodes.definition: The study of formal proofs as mathematical objects, including proof systems, consistency, normalization, and proof strength.
scope_excludes: Informal proof-writing advice

nodes.definition: The study of classical Euclidean figures and theorems involving incidence, congruence, similarity, angles, circles, and metric relations.
scope_excludes: Coordinate methods as the primary representation

nodes.definition: The study of geometric figures and relations represented by coordinates, equations, vectors, and transformations in Euclidean spaces.
scope_excludes: Abstract algebraic varieties

nodes.definition: The study of smooth curves and surfaces through parametrization, curvature, tangent spaces, metrics, and local or global geometric properties.
scope_excludes: Elementary plane geometry without smooth structure
